issues.description: The problem statement and UML consistently refer to a Stock class and require the SealSaloon.stock attribute to be of type Stock, but the template repository provides a fully implemented Inventory class (with add/take/find/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock methods) and an empty Stock.java file. The solution implementation uses Inventory as the type for the shared stock attribute (private static final Inventory stock). This naming/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory, and the presence of an empty Stock.java) creates a structural inconsistency that will confuse students: they are instructed to work with/modify a Stock class but the working implementation is named Inventory. Students may implement a Stock class or try to modify the existing Stock.java while the provided Inventory contains the necessary functionality, leading to duplication or compile/type errors relative to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the type/name used for the shared stock across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) rename Inventory.java to Stock.java and remove the empty Stock.java so the class expected by the spec exists in the template, updating references accordingly; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and document that Inventory is the stock implementation. Ensure the template contains a single, correctly named class matching the specification to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (the saloon's inventory), but the provided template and the solution use/implement a class named 'Inventory' to provide the exact same functionality (methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). Additionally, an empty Stock.java file exists in the template/solution trees which increases confusion. This mismatched naming for the same core concept (the shared ingredient storage) creates a cognitive mapping barrier: students are told to modify/use 'Stock' in the exercise text but the concrete implementation and examples use 'Inventory'.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the shared inventory concept across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (Inventory.java -> Stock.java), update all references (in SealSaloon and elsewhere) to use Stock, and remove the empty Stock.java stub; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock'. This alignment will eliminate the mapping confusion for students.
